title: Fix two notes before the ferry leaves
summary: One note says 9:15. Another says 9:50. Find the time you would tell a friend.
where: Use the green Practice desk on this page. It works on an iPad or computer. You can do this whole task offline.

actions.title: Read the schedule
actions.do: Tap schedule.txt. Read the pier number and the time.
actions.see: Find Pier 6 and 9:15 a.m. on the same line.
actions.stuck: Tap the file name once. Its words appear in the result area.

actions.title: Spot the mismatch
actions.do: Tap notice.txt. Compare the minutes with the schedule.
actions.see: The notice says 9:50. Someone trusting it would arrive 35 minutes late.
actions.stuck: Read the last two digits in each time.

actions.title: Fix the notice
actions.do: Choose the time the schedule supports. Then read the new notice.
actions.see: It now says 9:15 a.m. The pier number is still 6.
actions.stuck: A wrong pick gives a hint. You can pick again.

actions.title: Check the rest
actions.do: Open both notes again. Look at the pier, time and packing tip.
actions.see: The times match. The tip about a hat is still there.
actions.stuck: Press Start practice again if you want another turn.

roles: Check a mail report against one sample row.
Check an invite against the meeting note.
Test one change in a game.
sources: Read more about files and folders

title: Open Devin beside the book
summary: A tab keeps a page open. Use two tabs so you can switch back to the directions.
where: Use Safari, Chrome or Edge. Keep this book in your first tab.

actions.title: Find your browser
actions.do: On iPad swipe down on the Home Screen and search for Safari. On Mac press Command and Space and type Safari. On Windows open Start and type Edge.
actions.see: You see a window with a long address box.
actions.stuck: Choose the app with that name in your device’s search results.

actions.title: Open a new tab
actions.do: On Mac press Command and T. On Windows press Ctrl and T. On iPad use the tabs button, then the plus sign.
actions.see: The book stays in one tab. A blank tab opens beside it.
actions.stuck: If the book disappears, tap the tabs button to see open pages.

actions.title: Go to Devin
actions.do: Tap the address box. Type https://app.devin.ai/ and press Go or Enter.
actions.see: Devin opens. It may ask you to sign in.
actions.stuck: If you get a list of search results, try the full address again in the address box.

actions.title: Go back to the book
actions.do: Choose the tab called All About Devin. Switch back and forth once.
actions.see: You can follow the book while the tool stays open.
actions.stuck: If you opened the book from your Home Screen, use the app switcher instead.

roles: Keep the mail help page open beside a report.
Follow a Teams guide in a second tab.
See the app and its directions at once.

title: Make a home for your practice files
summary: A folder is like an envelope for files. Make an empty one you can find again.
where: Use Finder on a Mac, File Explorer on Windows or Files on an iPad. Make the folder on the device that will run your tool.

actions.title: Open the file app
actions.do: Click the blue Finder face on Mac. On Windows press the Windows key and E. On iPad find Files and tap Browse.
actions.see: You see places where files are kept.
actions.stuck: If iPad shows Recent, tap Browse to pick a place.

actions.title: Pick a place
actions.do: Open Documents on a computer or On My iPad on an iPad. Read the name of the place.
actions.see: You know where to look tomorrow.
actions.stuck: Choose a folder you control if this one belongs to a shared team.

actions.title: Make the folder
actions.do: On Mac choose File, then New Folder. On Windows choose New, then Folder. On iPad open More and choose New Folder. Call it Harbor Notes.
actions.see: Harbor Notes appears in the list.
actions.stuck: If that name is in use, add the word Practice.

actions.title: Find it again
actions.do: Open Harbor Notes. Go back one level. Find the folder by name and open it again.
actions.see: You can return to the same empty folder twice.
actions.stuck: If you lose the folder, search for Harbor Notes and open it by name.

roles: Keep fake mail rows and their report together.
Keep a sample agenda beside its notes.
Give a score app its own folder.

title: Unpack the practice kit
summary: A ZIP holds several files in one package. Take the files out before you run a lab.
where: Open the first Devin lab and find the practice kit link. Use a computer with PowerShell to run the later tests.

actions.title: Save the ZIP
actions.do: Tap Download the practice kit. Pick Downloads if the browser asks for a place.
actions.see: Find exchange-inventory.zip in Downloads.
actions.stuck: Use the browser’s recent downloads list to show where it went.

actions.title: Open the bundle
actions.do: On Windows right-click the ZIP and choose Extract All. On Mac double-click it. In Files on iPad tap it once.
actions.see: A regular folder appears. Some browsers open the ZIP for you.
actions.stuck: If you are still looking inside a ZIP on Windows, choose Extract All.

actions.title: Find the table
actions.do: Open the new folder. Find mailboxes.csv and README.md. A CSV holds rows of data.
actions.see: You can point to a sample table and a separate set of directions.
actions.stuck: Look inside the inner folder if the first folder has just one item.

actions.title: Look at the test
actions.do: Open README.md as text. Find Test-Inventory.ps1 in the directions. Leave the sample rows as supplied.
actions.see: You have found the test file. The next lab shows how to run it.
actions.stuck: Use a text editor or a file preview if the README asks for an app.

roles: Find the fake mailbox list for your report.
Unpack a set of training notes.
Give players a game and its rules together.

title: Ask your computer which folder is open
summary: A terminal is a place to type a short instruction. Start with two questions that only read information.
where: Open the unpacked Exchange practice folder on a Mac or Windows computer. On iPad, use the offline Practice desk to explore the sample files.

actions.title: Open the window
actions.do: On a Mac press Command and Space. Type Terminal and press Return. On Windows open Start, type PowerShell, and open it.
actions.see: A cursor blinks after a short line of text.
actions.stuck: Use the app search on the computer if a web search opens instead.

actions.title: Find your folder
actions.do: On Mac type pwd and press Return. On Windows type Get-Location and press Enter.
actions.see: A line shows the folder you are in.
actions.stuck: Copy just the command for your kind of computer.

actions.title: Read the names
actions.do: On Mac type ls and press Return. On Windows type Get-ChildItem and press Enter.
actions.see: The command lists the names in your current folder. In the kit folder you can find mailboxes.csv.
actions.stuck: A long list is fine. Read its last few lines.

actions.title: Finish the turn
actions.do: Wait for the cursor to return. Close the window once both questions have answers.
actions.see: You read your location and a list of files. Neither command changed a file.
actions.stuck: To cancel an unfinished command, hold Control and press C.

roles: Find the folder for a mail report.
Find a sample file for a meeting guide.
See which files make up your game.

title: Catch an answer that sounds right
summary: Does a ferry ticket cost five coins? The only way to tell is to find the price in the note.
where: In Ask Devin, use only this practice note: Saturday ferry. Pier 6. Meet at 9:15 a.m. Bring a hat. The same note appears in the offline Practice desk.

actions.title: Ask a question with proof
actions.do: Ask where and when to meet. Use only the note. Underline the words that answer you.
actions.see: Pier 6 and 9:15 a.m. both appear in the note.
actions.stuck: If a city appears, ask which word in the note names it.

actions.title: Ask what is missing
actions.do: Ask what the ticket costs. Ask the helper to say unknown if the note leaves it out.
actions.see: The answer should be unknown.
actions.stuck: If you get a price, ask for the exact line that gives it.

actions.title: Change one fact
actions.do: Make a fresh copy with the time changed to 10:30 a.m. Ask where and when again in a new chat.
actions.see: The pier stays 6. The time changes to 10:30.
actions.stuck: Check you pasted the newer copy before you ask again.

actions.title: Check your new note
actions.do: Write a one-line reminder for a friend. Check its day, time and pier against your latest copy.
actions.see: Every detail in the reminder has a source.
actions.stuck: Check one fact at a time if the full line is hard to compare.

roles: Check a mailbox count by hand.
Check a date before sending an invite.
Test that a score changes only when it should.
sources: Mozilla on browsing and finding a source

title: Choose Ask, a project folder or an Agent session
summary: Decide when you need a quick answer, a place to keep files or an agent to edit them.
where: Use Ask Devin and a practice repo, a project folder with saved history. You can also read the sample notes in the offline Practice desk.

actions.title: Try one question
actions.do: In Ask Devin, try “Make these four words shorter: Meet at the dock.” Read the reply.
actions.see: Meet at dock is short. You can decide whether it sounds natural.
actions.stuck: If a time appears, ask again and tell it to keep the same facts.

actions.title: Gather files
actions.do: In a practice repo, save three text files. The schedule says noon, the notice says ten and the packing list says to bring a map.
actions.see: All three items belong to one named place.
actions.stuck: Give each note a clear name before you add it to a project.

actions.title: Give an agent a job
actions.do: Open an Agent session on that practice repo. Ask it to fix only the notice. Inspect the changed line before accepting it.
actions.see: The notice now says noon. The schedule and packing list stay the same.
actions.stuck: If it wants to rewrite everything, narrow the job to one line in the notice.

actions.title: Pick for yourself
actions.do: For each job, name your starting place: explain a word, store three notes, or edit a file and show the change.
actions.see: Ask Devin can explain the word. The repo keeps the notes. The Agent session can edit the notice.
actions.stuck: When two tools fit, choose the one whose result you can check.

roles: Use a project for mail report files.
Keep related meeting notes together.
Ask an agent to fix one broken score button.
sources: GitHub’s introduction to a shared project

title: Read the old line and the new one
summary: An edit can fix the time and break the pier number. Learn how to catch both.
where: Use the sample schedule and notice from the offline Practice desk. The schedule says Pier 6 at 9:15. A minus marks the old line. A plus marks its replacement.

actions.title: Check the time
actions.do: Compare Meet at Pier 6 at 9:50 with Meet at Pier 6 at 9:15. Point to the changed part.
actions.see: The minutes change from 50 to 15.
actions.stuck: Cover the words before the time and compare the final digits.

actions.title: Check the rest
actions.do: Try this replacement instead: Meet at Pier 8 at 9:15. Which extra detail moved?
actions.see: The pier changed to 8. The schedule still says 6.
actions.stuck: Hide the time with your finger and read the words that remain.

actions.title: Ask for one fix
actions.do: Write: Keep Pier 6. Fix only the minutes. Show the new line before saving.
actions.see: A small change is easy to compare with its source.
actions.stuck: If a tool has already made a practice edit, look at its change view before keeping it.

actions.title: Read the final file
actions.do: Open the edited notice. Ask someone to tell you the pier and time from that file alone.
actions.see: The reader can say Pier 6 at 9:15.
actions.stuck: If the old time appears, check whether you opened the old file or the changed copy.

roles: Review a mailbox filter before saving it.
Keep the right room when editing a meeting time.
Review a score fix before sharing the app.
sources: GitHub’s introduction to changes and review

title: Check which account is open
summary: A tool can have a personal space and a team space. Learn to tell them apart.
where: Open Devin in a browser using your approved training account. Use only pretend data in this exercise.

actions.title: Read the account menu
actions.do: Look in a corner for a picture or initials. Open the menu. Read the name of the active space.
actions.see: You can tell whether you opened a team space or a personal space.
actions.stuck: Look under Account or Settings if the picture is hidden.

actions.title: Pick a practice space
actions.do: Choose a place you control for a made-up note. Use this sample: The practice ferry leaves at ten.
actions.see: You know where that note would be saved.
actions.stuck: If the names look alike, ask the person who set up the account to show you the right space.

actions.title: Read the permission
actions.do: Suppose a helper wants to list calendar events. Look for words that say read or change. Which does this job need?
actions.see: Reading is enough to list what is there.
actions.stuck: If you cannot choose a smaller permission, leave the connection off and use a pretend note.

actions.title: Recognize a limit
actions.do: If you see Ask your admin, write down the feature and the space you chose. Try the book’s Practice desk while you check access.
actions.see: You can explain what is missing without guessing at a new button.
actions.stuck: Changing your prompt cannot unlock an account feature.

roles: Use pretend mail records in a practice space.
Check the selected team before opening notes.
Keep a personal game in its own workspace.

title: Tell a note from a picture or table
summary: The end of a file name is a clue to what is inside. Try four common kinds.
where: Use these pretend names: notice.txt, banner.png, guests.csv and notes.zip.

actions.title: Find a note
actions.do: Read the part after each dot. Pick the name most likely to hold a plain note.
actions.see: notice.txt is a good choice. The ending txt usually means text.
actions.stuck: If your device hides endings, look at the file details.

actions.title: Read a table
actions.do: Write Name,Pier on one line and Guest,6 on the next. Each comma starts the next column.
actions.see: Guest is in the Name column. The pier is 6.
actions.stuck: If an imported line stays in one box, choose comma as the divider.

actions.title: Pick a picture
actions.do: Choose the file you would preview for an app banner. Look at the preview before using it.
actions.see: banner.png is a picture file. The preview shows which picture it actually is.
actions.stuck: Renaming a text file to .png does not turn it into a picture.

actions.title: Choose one input
actions.do: A helper asks for the guest list. Choose guests.csv. If it came in a ZIP, unpack it first.
actions.see: You gave the helper the table it needs.
actions.stuck: Cancel the file picker and choose again if you tapped the wrong name.

roles: Use a table of fake mailbox rows.
Pick the right picture for a training note.
Keep game rules in text and artwork in image files.
